title: Introduction to barbac
text: build toy dataset 4 true barcodes, seeded 20-nucleotide random sequence, 100 noisy reads per barcode. read per-base substitution probability 1%.
code: alphabet <- c("A", "C", "G", "T")  random_barcode <- function(len = 20) {   paste0(sample(alphabet, len, replace = TRUE), collapse = "") }  mutate_seq <- function(seq, sub_rate = 0.01) {   bases <- strsplit(seq, "")[[1]]   hit   <- runif(length(bases)) < sub_rate   bases[hit] <- vapply(bases[hit], function(b) {     sample(setdiff(alphabet, b), 1L)   }, character(1))   paste0(bases, collapse = "") }  true_barcodes <- vapply(1:4, function(i) random_barcode(), character(1)) true_barcodes #> [1] "ATGACAGGCCGGAAACCCCG" "AGAAAACAACCCATGATGCC" "CCGTTTCTAGCATTAGTCCG" #> [4] "GCCTTCCACCCCAGGTCGGT"  reads <- unlist(lapply(true_barcodes, function(b) {   replicate(100, mutate_seq(b, sub_rate = 0.01)) }))  # Collapse to unique-sequence counts input <- as.data.frame(table(reads), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) names(input) <- c("barcode", "counts") input <- input[order(-input$counts), ] head(input) #>                 barcode counts #> 49 CCGTTTCTAGCATTAGTCCG     81 #> 5  AGAAAACAACCCATGATGCC     80 #> 21 ATGACAGGCCGGAAACCCCG     78 #> 61 GCCTTCCACCCCAGGTCGGT     77 #> 19 ATAACAGGCCGGAAACCCCG      3 #> 43 CCGTTTCAAGCATTAGTCCG      3

title: Introduction to barbac
text: super_cluster2() accepts either data.frame columns barcode counts, path CSV layout. pass data.frame directly use Levenshtein distance threshold 2. row one cluster: central_barcode abundance-ranked representative, all_barcodes all_counts member barcodes raw counts, sum_counts summed abundance. can check well clustering recovered true barcodes:
code: result <- super_cluster2(   input,   distance    = 2,   merge_ratio = 20,   verbose     = FALSE ) result #> # A tibble: 4 × 5 #>   cluster_id central_barcode      all_barcodes all_counts sum_counts #>   <chr>      <chr>                <list>       <list>          <int> #> 1 group1     CCGTTTCTAGCATTAGTCCG <chr [18]>   <int [18]>        100 #> 2 group2     AGAAAACAACCCATGATGCC <chr [18]>   <int [18]>        100 #> 3 group3     ATGACAGGCCGGAAACCCCG <chr [18]>   <int [18]>        100 #> 4 group4     GCCTTCCACCCCAGGTCGGT <chr [22]>   <int [22]>        100 recovered <- result$central_barcode sum(true_barcodes %in% recovered)     # how many true barcodes are centroids #> [1] 4 setdiff(true_barcodes, recovered)     # any missed #> character(0)

title: Introduction to barbac
text: barbac_ts_area() takes table counts across timepoints returns stacked-area ggplot per-timepoint frequencies. accepts long-format input directly:  Lineage C illustrates “late arrivals” case: zero counts timepoints 0–7, carried full series include_late = TRUE (default) missing cells filled small ε. function auto-detects Bartender’s wide export layout:  layout neither long Bartender-wide, function stops clear error lists expected column names.
code: tp   <- 0:20                                            # 21 timepoints n_tp <- length(tp)  ts_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(   tibble(barcode = "A", time = tp,          counts = round(seq(1000, 200, length.out = n_tp))),    # falling   tibble(barcode = "B", time = tp,          counts = round(seq( 200, 1000, length.out = n_tp))),   # rising   tibble(barcode = "C", time = tp,          counts = ifelse(tp < 8, 0,                          round(seq(0, 800, length.out = n_tp - 7 + 1))[-1])), # late arrival   tibble(barcode = "D", time = tp, counts = 50)                 # constant )  barbac_ts_area(ts_long, min_total_count = 0) set.seed(11)  ts_wide <- cbind(   tibble(     Cluster.ID    = sprintf("bc%02d", 1:5),     Center        = c("ACGT", "ACGA", "ACCA", "TGGT", "GACC"),     Cluster.Score = round(runif(5, 0.7, 1), 2)   ),   setNames(     as.data.frame(matrix(rpois(5 * 20, 100), nrow = 5)),     sprintf("time_point_%d", 1:20)   ) )  barbac_ts_area(ts_wide, min_total_count = 0)

title: Introduction to barbac
text: Set interactive = TRUE get interactive widget hover tooltips revealing barcode identifier, timepoint frequency whichever band cursor . Two backends supported: interactive = TRUE (default interactivity requested) "ggiraph" uses ggiraph: preserves exact ggplot look, snappy hover stacked areas, lightweight SVG output. interactive = "plotly" uses plotly: built-zoom / pan / lasso, slightly heavier bundle minor theme drift. static interactive paths accept exactly arguments; return type differs (ggplot versus girafe plotly htmlwidget).

title: Introduction to barbac
text: four-lineage toy demonstrates API. practice barbac_ts_area() designed handle many-lineage output real barcode-sequencing experiment. simulate 100-lineage community across 21 timepoints, log-normal initial abundances small Gaussian fitness effect per lineage, plot every lineage using minou palette ltc package.  Every timepoint fills stack y = 1 exactly. Lineages positive fitness sweep upward across 21 timepoints; negative-fitness lineages shrink; neutral ones drift proportionally initial abundance. ltc package available GitHub via remotes::install_github("loukesio/ltc_palettes"). character vector colour hex codes works palette, viridisLite::magma(), RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(), manual palette, source equally valid.
code: set.seed(7)  n_bar   <- 100 tp      <- 0:20                       # 21 timepoints depth   <- 1e6  barcodes  <- sprintf("bc_%03d", seq_len(n_bar)) fitness   <- rnorm(n_bar, mean = 0, sd = 0.20) init_freq <- rlnorm(n_bar, meanlog = 0, sdlog = 1.5) init_freq <- init_freq / sum(init_freq)  ts_multi <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tp, function(t) {   raw   <- init_freq * exp(fitness * t)   freq  <- raw / sum(raw)   tibble::tibble(     barcode = barcodes,     time    = t,     counts  = round(freq * depth)   ) }))  # One colour per barcode, interpolated from the minou seed palette # (same pattern as the phage.colors helper in the ltc README). phage_colors <- function(df) {   n <- dplyr::n_distinct(df$barcode)   pal <- if (requireNamespace("ltc", quietly = TRUE)) {     ltc::ltc("minou", n, type = "continuous")   } else {     viridisLite::magma(n, begin = 0.05, end = 0.95)  # fallback   }   grDevices::colorRampPalette(pal)(n) }  barbac_ts_area(   ts_multi,   min_total_count = 0,                            # plot every lineage   palette         = phage_colors(ts_multi),   title           = "Multilineage — 100 barcodes across 21 timepoints" )

title: Introduction to barbac
text: diversity static plot useful overall shape useless identifying individual lineages. Setting interactive = TRUE returns interactive widget per-band hover tooltips showing barcode identifier, timepoint frequency. barbac_ts_area() supports two interactive backends: interactive = TRUE ("ggiraph", default) — renders via ggiraph, preserves exact ggplot look, produces lightweight SVG-based widget, performs well hundreds stacked polygons. interactive = "plotly" — renders via plotly’s ggplotly(), gives built-zoom / pan / lasso cost slightly drifted theme heavier HTML page. prefer plotly’s zoom / pan controls:
code: barbac_ts_area(   ts_multi,   min_total_count = 0,   palette         = phage_colors(ts_multi),   title           = "Multilineage — hover over a band for its barcode",   interactive     = TRUE                                # = "ggiraph" ) barbac_ts_area(   ts_multi,   min_total_count = 0,   palette         = phage_colors(ts_multi),   title           = "Multilineage (plotly backend)",   interactive     = "plotly" )

title: Introduction to barbac
text: Briefly: algorithm sorts input sequences descending abundance, scans sequence candidate centroids within edit distance distance using two-tier Hamming/Levenshtein index, scores candidates count-aware log-likelihood, either merges sequence best-scoring parent (subject distance-aware count-ratio guard) seeds new cluster. post-hoc refinement pass promotes -represented children large clusters reassigns neighbours. Johnson et al. (2023) 100k-barcode benchmark super_cluster2() matches Shepherd four Johnson metrics (Pearson R, FN%, FP%, WS%) running roughly 1.7× faster. indel errors added simulator — Shepherd’s Hamming-based index struggles — super_cluster2()’s wrong-sequence rate stays order magnitude Shepherd’s. Reproducibility scripts live benchmark/ directory package repository.

title: barbac - DNA barcode lineage analysis
text: barbac (barcode bioinformatics analysis clustering) R package end--end DNA barcode lineage tracking. provides lightweight wrapper around bioinformatics pipeline used extract barcodes FASTQ reads (FastQC → PEAR → minimap2 → samtools) native R clustering routine, super_cluster2(), backed bit-parallel 64-bit edit-distance kernel written C++. Johnson et al. (2023) reference benchmark, barbac reaches statistical parity Shepherd ~1.7× speed; datasets indel errors substantially outperforms Shepherd false-positive wrong-sequence rates.

what: Parity with Shepherd on the Johnson et al. (2023) reference dataset
title: barbac - DNA barcode lineage analysis
text: input (100,000 true barcodes, ~1.5M unique reads), parameters (max distance 3), evaluation protocol. 470 471 false negatives shared two methods — fail hard cases (mostly barcodes count = 0 input). See benchmark/compare_with_shepherd.ipynb full analysis.

title: barbac - DNA barcode lineage analysis
text: benchmarked barbac Shepherd, Starcode, Bartender 10,000-barcode / 1M-read datasets Illumina-quality error regimes typical experimental-evolution barcode sequencing: 0.5% per-base substitution rate, insertion+deletion rates 0% 0.5%. Higher indel rates typical long-read platforms (PacBio, nanopore) outside scope comparison. Wall = end--end wall time. Algo = pure clustering time, excluding R boot + package loading barbac (Shepherd/Starcode/Bartender pay negligible boot tax wall ≈ algo ). -indel baseline. four methods statistically indistinguishable (R = 1.0000, FN/FP/WS within 5 barcodes 10,000). Confirms four-way validity check. Realistic Illumina indel regime (0.5%). Two-tier picture: barbac Starcode essentially tied clustering accuracy — preserve R = 1.0000 confine WS ~1.6%. use Levenshtein natively. Shepherd Bartender break. Shepherd’s WS rises 113-fold 48.81% (31-fold gap versus barbac); Bartender’s rises 509.41% (324-fold gap). rely Hamming-based indexing fragments indel variants spurious centroids. barbac beats Levenshtein peer (Starcode). ~7× faster algorithm time (2.4 s vs 17.2 s low_indel; wall-time gap smaller barbac pays fixed ~3 s R-boot tax Starcode ). R-native, -package Rcpp binding — shelling standalone C binary parsing text output. Integrated FASTQ→lineage pipeline (run_cli_pipeline, barbac_xtr) time-series visualisation (barbac_ts_area) package. Full reproducibility scripts benchmark/indel_experiment/. experiment runner also produces mid- high-indel conditions; regimes (2%+ indels) outside Illumina scope current paper treated future work.
